findings.observation: Highest-impact mandatory failure: at the pinned revision, a synthetic family-B receipt is associated with a private product owned by family A through an exact alias. The local isolation probe fails while the 34-test regression passes. This is a demonstrated internal normalization boundary failure, not evidence of a production incident.
findings.nextAction: Owner: Family Ledger maintainer. Define global versus family-private catalog/alias visibility, then implement tenant-aware exact, fuzzy and IA resolution plus family-aware price/query paths in a separately approved change. Preserve this failing packet as the baseline.
findings.closureCheck: Retain the exact OBL-006 counterexample and require it to pass after the fix; challenge exact/fuzzy/IA matching with two families, allow explicitly shared global products, and reject cross-family private associations. Add a PostgreSQL integration case and verify unchanged legitimate same-family normalization before claiming broader isolation.

findings.observation: OBL-003 has convincing static assignment code and a passing queue test, but the supplied executed assertions do not verify every unmatched line's description, raw text and monetary amount. The method name 'preserves_everything' is stronger than the measured assertions.
findings.nextAction: Owner: receipt-ingestion maintainer. Add an independent preservation test that retrieves every persisted unmatched ReceiptLine and compares its source description/raw_text/line_total while checking the corresponding review entry.
findings.closureCheck: At a named revision, show field-by-field equality for multiple unmatched lines with different amounts, non-ASCII descriptions and mixed units, and a negative control that drops or mutates an amount must fail the test.

findings.observation: Application confirmation/query and event-driven inventory are documented targets without executed end-to-end delivery evidence. Internal session writes, a prototype UI and the checked transcription do not demonstrate these flows.
findings.nextAction: Owner: application/API maintainer. Keep OBL-005 and OBL-007 pending and define bounded confirmation, authenticated query, transaction and duplicate-event contracts before connecting the flows.
findings.closureCheck: Produce independently checked HTTP-to-PostgreSQL confirmation/query receipts and an event-redelivery case with unchanged inventory after duplicate delivery; include rollback and authorization cases.

findings.observation: The packet supplies output hashes and source revisions which reviewer B checked locally, but an aggregate pytest receipt and the static trace labels do not establish a complete per-obligation evidence chain or externally authenticated results.
findings.nextAction: Owner: SDD evidence maintainer. Preserve local-run provenance, add timestamp/input/environment digests and named per-check result mapping, and keep diagnostic review distinct from CI authority and organizational scoring.
findings.closureCheck: A later reviewer can follow each measured obligation to its selected rule, source revision, check logic and immutable input/output receipt, while unsupported obligations remain NOT_EVALUATED and reconstruction remains NOT_TESTED.
